validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/DUPLICATE all checked and confirmed independent of GEM/gem.wiki. The '261 Upgrade Project(s)' is a real Tennessee Gas Pipeline Company, LLC (TGP, a Kinder Morgan subsidiary) NGA section 7(b)/7(c) certificate project: TGP filed the application on October 19, 2018 (FERC Docket CP19-7-000; Federal Register Notice of Application, 2018-11-08), FERC issued a Notice of Intent to prepare an EA (2018-12-12) and a Notice of Availability of the EA (2019-05-24), the certificate matter appeared on the Commission's Dec 19, 2019 Sunshine Act meeting agenda (item C-6, CP19-7-000), a Section 4(d) rate filing for 'the 261 Upgrade Project' effective 11/1/2020 confirms Phase 1 in-service, and EIA's independently-compiled Natural Gas Pipeline Projects tracker (todayinenergy article id=50376, and the downloadable historical-projects workbook, row 'Project Name = 261 Upgrade Projects') both independently confirm the project reached full completion on October 6, 2021 (Phase 2/final phase, adding an upgraded compressor at Station 261 in Agawam, MA). Three independent origin families (FERC/Federal Register regulatory notices, EIA's analyst-written todayinenergy article, and EIA's separately-compiled workbook) cross-confirm Capacity (~72.4 MMcf/d vs GEM's 72.00, within rounding), Length (2.1 mi = 3.38 km vs GEM's 3.40 km), Diameter (12 in, exact), SegmentCost ($5.53M, exact match to GEM's $5,530,000), start/completion date (Oct 6, 2021, exact match to GEM's StartYear1/StartMonth1=2021-10), and Docket CP19-7. Checked against the 45-row deepsweep-remainder roster and against P0259 (the TGP system-level row already swept in batch 1, context only, never cited as a ref for this segment row) -- no duplicate or relabeling found; this is a genuine, distinct, segment-level project entry. CAVEAT: the sheet's own cited Status ref candidate (kindermorgan.com/.../261_upgrade.aspx) is confirmed dead (live 404; Wayback CDX shows it was NEVER captured with real content, only redirect/404 snapshots from 2021-2024) -- a genuinely-gone page per standing rule 3, replaced below with independently-verified refs, not merely Wayback-annotated.

fills.researcher_notes: No single document explicitly labels this project 'delayed', so DelayType correctly stays 'inferred' -- but the inference is well supported: application filed Oct 2018, EA not available until May 2019 (7 months), the certificate matter was still on the Commission's full-meeting Sunshine Act agenda (not delegated-authority-approved) in Dec 2019 (~14 months post-application) amid documented off-the-record Senate constituent communications on the docket, and the project then completed in two separate phases (~Nov 2020 and Oct 2021) rather than one. That combination -- an elongated, politically-watched certificate process plus phased construction -- is consistent with a real, if undocumented-by-name, delay relative to a routine small-loop timeline. Tier medium (inference from process-timeline evidence, not a dated 'delay' statement) with two independent FERC-docket origins plus the Sunshine Act notice.

summary: P2496 (Tennessee Gas Pipeline / '261 Upgrade Project') is a real, fully-completed FERC NGA section 7 project (Docket CP19-7-000, filed Oct 19, 2018 by Tennessee Gas Pipeline Company LLC, a Kinder Morgan subsidiary): a 2.1-mile/12-inch loop plus a compressor replacement at Station 261 in Agawam, MA, completed in two phases (~Nov 2020, final Oct 6, 2021) confirmed independently by EIA's todayinenergy article, EIA's historical-projects workbook, and multiple Federal Register/FERC notices. Staged REFS_ADDED on 12 units (Status, Fuel, PipelineType, Proposal, Start, Delay, Capacity, Length, Diameter, Location, SegmentCost, Operator, Owner -- 13 counted; see fills[] for exact list) plus 1 existence/no-change validity confirmation and 1 attribution concern: GEM's Location cluster records the project's second endpoint as a repeat of the Massachusetts start (Agawam again), but two independent FERC dockets and the EIA workbook agree the project's actual Connecticut endpoint is Suffield, CT -- proposed correction EndState/Province=Connecticut, EndPrefecture/District=Suffield. Construction[ref], Pressure, and FuelSource are genuinely UNRESOLVED: no source gives a specific construction-start month, an MAOP/pressure figure for this segment, or a single attributable upstream fuel source for what is a mainline transmission-network upgrade (FuelSource correctly stays blank per the schema gotcha, not forced). Owner and SegmentCost are filled at medium tier (single independent origin each) with notes on what a second-source search covered.
